_comment: Figures and rules transcribed from the documents in sources/ for data/education-parameters.json. Every amount in this corpus is statutory; none is inflation adjusted through 2026, so the documents are the enacted laws and the 2024 edition of the Code with its amendment and effective-date notes.

_sources.usc-26-530: 26 U.S.C. 530 (2024 edition of the United States Code), including the Pub. L. 107-16 amendment notes
_sources.usc-26-127: 26 U.S.C. 127 (2024 edition of the United States Code), including the Pub. L. 106-170, 107-16, 116-136 and 116-260 amendment notes
_sources.usc-26-529: 26 U.S.C. 529 (2024 edition of the United States Code), including the Pub. L. 115-97, 116-94 and 117-328 effective-date notes
_sources.pl-104-188: Small Business Job Protection Act of 1996, Pub. L. 104-188, sections 1202 (IRC 127) and 1806 (IRC 529)
_sources.pl-105-34: Taxpayer Relief Act of 1997, Pub. L. 105-34, sections 213 (IRC 530) and 221 (IRC 127)
_sources.pl-107-16: Economic Growth and Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2001, Pub. L. 107-16, sections 401 (IRC 530) and 411 (IRC 127)
_sources.pl-111-312: Tax Relief, Unemployment Insurance Reauthorization, and Job Creation Act of 2010, Pub. L. 111-312, section 101(a)(1) (EGTRRA sunset moved to December 31, 2012)
_sources.pl-112-240: American Taxpayer Relief Act of 2012, Pub. L. 112-240, section 101(a) (EGTRRA title IX struck)
_sources.pl-119-21: Pub. L. 119-21, sections 70412 (IRC 127 indexing after 2026) and 70413(b) (IRC 529 elementary and secondary limit to $20,000)

1996.educationalAssistance_source: pl-104-188 section 1202(a) extends IRC 127 through May 31, 1997, for taxable years beginning after December 31, 1994 (section 1202(c)(1)); the $5,250 is IRC 127(a)(2), usc-26-127
1996.qualifiedTuitionProgram_source: pl-104-188 section 1806(c)(1): "The amendments made by this section shall apply to taxable years ending after the date of the enactment of this Act" (August 20, 1996). A 1996 taxable year may end on or before that date, so whether IRC 529 applies depends on when the taxable year ends. IRC 529(b)(6) states no dollar limit; see usc-26-529.
1996.coverdell_source: pl-105-34 section 213(f) applies IRC 530 to taxable years beginning after December 31, 1997

See usc-26-529.
2023.coverdell_source: pl-107-16 section 401(a)(1) substitutes $2,000 for $500 and section 401(b) substitutes $190,000 and $30,000 in IRC 530(c)(1), for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2001; continued past the EGTRRA sunset by pl-111-312 section 101(a)(1) and pl-112-240 section 101(a); usc-26-530
2023.qtpElementarySecondaryExpense_source: IRC 529(e)(3) last sentence, $10,000, added by Pub. L. 115-97 section 11032(a)(2) for distributions made after December 31, 2017 (section 11032(b), quoted in the usc-26-529 notes)
2023.qtpElementarySecondaryExpenseScope_sourc: IRC 529(c)(7), added by Pub. L. 115-97 section 11032(a)(1) for distributions made after December 31, 2017: "expenses for tuition in connection with enrollment or attendance at an elementary or secondary public, private, or religious school" (usc-26-529); IRC 529(e)(3) caps "expenses described in subsection (c)(7)"
2023.qtpQualifiedEducationLoanLifetime_source: IRC 529(c)(9)(B), added by Pub. L. 116-94 div. O section 302(b)(1), applicable to distributions made after December 31, 2018 per the usc-26-529 effective-date note
